title: LedgerShield
subtitle: Observe. Verify. Recover. · an explainable resilience laboratory
description: A blockchain resilience research platform combining signed transfers, seeded network faults, explainable detection and trust, guarded recovery, and reproducible policy experiments in a live local observatory.
status: Implemented local research platform · source available
users: Developers and researchers examining signed ledger execution, consensus assumptions, evidence-backed recovery, and reproducible reinforcement-learning comparisons.
problem: Linked hashes alone do not establish reliable ledger execution or safe recovery. A research platform must show how authentication, quorum, fault evidence, policy choices, and measured outcomes interact under explicit assumptions.
solution: Follow a signed transfer through a seeded centralized consensus simulator, introduce bounded faults, inspect detection and trust provenance, approve a guarded recovery, and compare policies using recorded experiments.
technicalDetails: Ed25519 identities sign canonical transfer payloads with chain IDs and nonces. The execution core checks replay, balance, and signature validity, stages block transactions atomically, and verifies hash-linked history and Merkle roots.

A fixed-membership centralized simulator collects signed prepare/commit votes using floor(2N/3)+1 quorum. Seeded latency, jitter, loss, timeouts, and partitions affect measured simulator progress without claiming real peer-to-peer or formal PBFT execution.

Rule indicators and an Isolation Forest baseline produce structured evidence. Bounded decaying trust advises a recovery orchestrator with observe-only defaults, human approval, quorum guards, cooldowns, idempotency, verification, and rollback.

React/Vite renders ten connected observatory pages over FastAPI REST and WebSockets. SQLAlchemy/Alembic retain public research records in PostgreSQL or SQLite; restart keeps archives but starts a fresh paused simulator.
Explicit offline Gymnasium/NumPy DQN training and matched policy evaluation retain seeds and checkpoint provenance. The live API uses a rule policy; learned policies are not deployed automatically.

challenges: A centralized educational research simulator, not a production financial network: no real peer-to-peer replicas, formally verified Byzantine safety, complete PBFT view changes, or durable live-consensus restart is implemented.
No public deployment or published GitHub release was available at review. Run the API and dashboard locally or use the documented Compose stack; no installer or hosted demo is claimed.

The live API uses a rule policy; DQN training and checkpoint evaluation are explicit offline work. The recorded learned policy did not outperform the no-healing baseline. Synthetic anomaly performance and simulator timing are not real-world security accuracy or hardware benchmarks.

Local operator/admin bearer tokens and process-local quotas do not provide deployment identity management or distributed abuse control. Research archives survive restarts, but active simulator state is volatile. Fresh rendered dashboard QA and independent security review remain outstanding.

caseStudy.architectureSummary: LedgerShield uses a React/Vite observatory and FastAPI service over one canonical signed ledger and seeded network simulator. Telemetry flows into rule/anomaly evidence, bounded trust, and mode-aware recovery guards. Reversible actions are verified against subsequent simulator progress and audited. Optional SQL archives preserve public research records, while explicit offline DQN experiments remain separate from the live rule-based control loop.

features.title: Authenticate intent before execution
features.description: Ed25519 signatures bind integer transfers to public-key identities, chain IDs, and nonces. Replay, duplicate, signature, and balance checks precede ordered atomic execution. Blocks commit to parent hashes, ordered transactions, Merkle roots, and genesis configuration; integrity checks replay the ledger state.

features.title: Make network assumptions observable
features.description: Fixed validator membership and signed prepare/commit certificates use a quorum that never shrinks for missing participants. Seeded delay, jitter, loss, partitions, wrong-hash votes, abstention, and bounded leader replacement produce inspectable stalls and counters inside a centralized simulator.

features.title: Explain evidence and trust changes
features.description: Rule checks and a synthetic-data Isolation Forest baseline expose method, severity, confidence, features, and raw evidence. Trust scores are bounded, time-decayed, and deduplicated with before/after records. Anomaly indicators are not proof of intent and cannot independently authorize quarantine.

features.title: Recover through explicit safeguards
features.description: Observe-only is the default. Approval-required and autonomous-simulation modes add expiring proposals, current-state guard rechecks, evidence requirements, fixed-quorum protection, cooldowns, retry budgets, and idempotent action keys. Disruptive actions verify progress and roll back a failed attempt.

features.title: Inspect a connected local observatory
features.description: Ten pages connect overview, network, ledger, security, trust, healing, RL, simulation, reports, and audit settings to the real local API. A reconnecting stream detects silence, rejects malformed state, and prevents an older HTTP response from overwriting a newer snapshot.

features.title: Compare policies without hiding outcomes
features.description: Explicit offline NumPy DQN training uses replay and a target network in a seeded Gymnasium environment. Matched application experiments compare no-healing, rule, and trained-DQN policies with shared configuration, disjoint evaluation seeds, raw rows, conditional timing, and exploratory uncertainty.

features.title: Retain research evidence across restarts
features.description: SQLAlchemy and Alembic preserve public blocks, transfers, alerts, trust updates, scenarios, audits, and completed experiments in PostgreSQL or SQLite. Transactional batches and complete pagination retain evidence, while archived snapshots remain historical records rather than resumable live consensus checkpoints.

decisions.title: Prefer explicit simulator assumptions
decisions.description: Keep one canonical execution model, fixed membership, verified signed votes, and seeded transport behavior so experiments expose exactly what is being measured. Quorum requirements remain unchanged when nodes fail or are quarantined.
decisions.tradeoff: The system supports repeatable research but cannot establish the safety or throughput of independently running distributed replicas or a production Byzantine protocol.

decisions.title: Separate indicators from authority
decisions.description: Retain evidence provenance and bounded advisory trust, then require mode, approval, quorum, reachability, and retry checks at action execution. Verify a new commit before reporting recovery and retain attempted outcomes when rollback is necessary.
decisions.tradeoff: Conservative guards can refuse an intervention or leave a fault unresolved; that outcome remains visible rather than weakening the simulator safety constraints to improve a recovery count.

decisions.title: Keep learning outside the live control path
decisions.description: Use explicit offline DQN training with checkpoint provenance and matched seeded comparison. The API remains on a rule policy and does not automatically train, load, or deploy learned weights.
decisions.tradeoff: Offline evaluation enables reproducibility but differs from the alert-driven application distribution. A learned model is not assumed to outperform a baseline or be safe for automatic deployment.

decisions.title: Archive evidence without claiming state recovery
decisions.description: Persist public research records in SQL transactions while keeping the active simulator single-process and volatile. Database failure is visible and pauses the simulator instead of silently discarding research evidence.
decisions.tradeoff: Completed records survive restarts, but the running ledger starts paused from fresh state. Resumable distributed consensus needs a different persistence and recovery design.

title: MathLens
subtitle: From a question to understanding · mathematics made inspectable
description: A live mathematics and model-analysis workbench with explainable numerical tools, interactive learning, a live arXiv feed, and experimental desktop and Android downloads.
users: Students, educators, and developers exploring how mathematical methods produce results, model metrics, and visual explanations.
problem: Mathematics and machine-learning demos often hide the calculation, data split, numerical limits, or assumptions behind a final number. Learners need to inspect both the result and how it was computed.
solution: Connect bounded server-side numerical methods to an interactive workspace with plots, deterministic explanations, held-out model metrics, worked lessons, puzzles, exports, and source-linked research.
technicalDetails: Native browser ES modules and SVG plots connect to a dependency-free Node.js HTTP core. The same request handler serves local development and a Vercel function; no React framework or external inference provider is required by the web core.

Householder QR least squares uses seeded splits and training-only scaling. Binary one-feature logistic regression, two-feature K-means and PCA expose computed metrics and explicit limits rather than general-purpose AutoML claims.
The allowlisted polynomial parser never evaluates arbitrary JavaScript. Bounded calculus, bisection, integration, matrix tools and statistics share request validation and finite numeric constraints.
Electron and Java WebView packages open the hosted workspace. They require internet, do not bundle offline computation, and keep local progress separate across clients.
features: Nine lessons and ten puzzle categories

flowchart LR
  Browser[Browser ES modules / online clients] --> API[Node JSON API / Vercel function]
  API --> Math[Bounded polynomial and numerical methods]
  API --> Models[QR / logistic / K-means / PCA]
  Math --> Plots[SVG plots and JSON exports]
  Models --> Plots
  Browser --> Local[(Browser-local learning records)]
  API --> Research[Bounded arXiv retrieval and cache]
  API --> Auth[Optional Supabase GoTrue adapter]
challenges: This is a working alpha with a published prerelease. General symbolic algebra, multifeature model pipelines, SHAP, generative explanations, durable jobs, and account-synced progress are not implemented.

Optional Supabase authentication requires owner configuration. Learning progress, bookmarks, and experiment metadata remain browser-local; uploaded numeric data are not persisted as a server-side dataset library.

Native downloads are experimental online clients: Windows is unsigned, Android uses debug signing, and Linux distribution coverage is limited. Android exports and email callbacks use Open in browser. No offline engine, updater, store release, or iOS binary is provided.

The repository reports 49 mathematical/API tests and successful native CI smoke checks. Expanded layouts still need rendered interaction checks; process-local quotas are not distributed abuse protection.

title: NeuroMap AI
subtitle: Research in focus · images, experiments, and traceable results
description: A private research workspace for NIfTI image inspection, reproducible synthetic ML experiments, computed evaluation, and traceable reports, with Windows and Android release downloads.
users: Developers and researchers exploring bounded image inspection, synthetic ML methodology, and reproducible experiment records.
problem: Research tooling needs to make image geometry, experimental assumptions, data partitions, and result provenance inspectable without conflating a synthetic demonstration with a clinical model.
solution: Connect validated image and synthetic-table intake to an authenticated workspace, bounded CPU analysis, interactive inspection, computed evaluation, and downloadable reports with provenance.
technicalDetails: The React/Vite workspace connects Three.js point-cloud and slice views to a FastAPI modular monolith. SQLAlchemy/Alembic and SQLite retain datasets, job states, checksums, reports, and audit records; private UUID-named payloads remain on the server.

The imaging path validates bounded single-file 3D NIfTI-1 volumes, checks spatial transforms and intensities, and exposes downsampled affine-positioned points and grayscale index slices. It does not perform segmentation or disease inference.

The synthetic classifier uses three artificial features, participant-grouped 60/20/20 splits, training-only scaling, validation-selected logistic regression, a dummy comparison, held-out metrics, and participant-cluster bootstrap intervals.
Windows and Android clients require an available frontend/API or configured HTTPS API. No public deployment, offline ML server, or iOS distribution installer is provided.

challenges: Research and education only: the classifier uses synthetic tabular features and labels. Image inspection does not diagnose disease, estimate clinical risk, segment anatomy, or provide clinically validated quality control.

No hosted public deployment is available. Windows and Android clients require a running server. The Windows publisher is unsigned; Android is release-signed, while device/emulator runtime testing and full installed Windows upgrade/uninstall testing remain pending. No iOS IPA is available.

The supported runtime is a single-owner, single-process workspace with a bounded CPU queue. Distributed workers, multi-tenant identity, production-scale throughput, and clinical validation remain outside this release.
